title: A Middle Gene Reveals Double Crossovers

scenes.tts: Two crossovers between the same pair of genes cancel out. How do you count what you cannot see? One crossover between two genes recombines them. A second crossover between the same two genes puts them back together. The gamete has been rearranged twice, and it looks parental.
scenes.visual: Two homologs, then one gamete slot marked with a question mark; a first crossover recombines the two outer genes, a second puts them back so the gamete reads parental.
scenes.narration: Two crossovers between the same pair of genes cancel out. How do you count what you cannot see? One crossover between two genes recombines them. A second crossover between the same two genes puts them back together. The gamete has been rearranged twice, and it looks parental.

scenes.tts: The fix is a third gene, placed between the other two. Call it the middle marker. Now a double crossover swaps only that middle gene. The two outer genes still look parental. But the middle gene has switched, and the hidden event shows.
scenes.visual: A middle gene appears between the outer two; the double-crossover gamete reads q + r, and the switched middle gene is ringed.
scenes.narration: The fix is a third gene, placed between the other two. Call it the middle marker. Now a double crossover swaps only that middle gene. The two outer genes still look parental. But the middle gene has switched, and the hidden event shows.

scenes.tts: A female carries three linked genes, P, Q and R, and is crossed to a tester. The tester adds only recessive alleles, so each offspring reads out one gamete from the mother. Sort one thousand offspring into eight classes. The two biggest classes have no crossover, and the four in the middle are single crossovers. The two smallest classes are usually the double crossovers, seven and five.
scenes.visual: Female and tester cross; eight bars of the lesson counts grow, then are coloured as parental, single and double.

scenes.tts: Match each rare class with the parental it most resembles. Each one differs at P and nowhere else. A double crossover swaps only the gene between the two crossovers. So P is the middle gene, and the order is Q, P, R. The order the names are written in tells you nothing.
scenes.visual: Each double beside its parental, the differing gene ringed; the letters then slide into map order with P in the middle.

scenes.tts: A double crossover is a crossover in each interval, so it counts in both. From Q to P, fifty-three and fifty-five singles plus twelve doubles make one hundred twenty in a thousand. That is twelve point zero centimorgans. From P to R, ninety-six and ninety-two singles plus the same twelve make two hundred, or twenty point zero. Together, Q to R is thirty-two point zero centimorgans.
scenes.visual: A map line with Q, P, R; twelve doubles feed both intervals; sums appear under each interval; the total appears.
scenes.caption: A double crossover is a crossover in each interval, so it counts in both. From Q to P, 53 and 55 singles plus 12 doubles make 120 in 1,000. That is 12.0 centimorgans. From P to R, 96 and 92 singles plus the same 12 make 200, or 20.0. Together, Q to R is 32.0 centimorgans.

scenes.tts: Now score only Q and R, as a two-point cross would. The doubles carry the parental combinations, so they drop out. Only the two hundred ninety-six singles count, which gives twenty-nine point six percent. That is two point four points short, the twelve doubles counted once in each interval. Count every double crossover in both intervals.
scenes.visual: A 32.0 bar of singles and doubles; the two-point bar loses the doubles and stops 2.4 short.
